item.title: Cabbie driving tests and looming national standards all on agenda for Blackburn with Darwen councillors

item.title: METER MISUSE: Glasgow taxi driver refused new licence after overcharging complaints
item.description: A Glasgow taxi driver who was suspended after complaints of overcharging passengers has been refused a new licence, with councillors concluding his conduct undermined public trust in the trade. Arsalan Khan lost his bid to renew his taxi driver’s licence for a further three years after appearing before the city’s licensing committee, which heard he had previously been suspended for charging incorrect fares and failing to use his meter. item.title: MAJORITY OF COMPLAINTS AND ENFORCEMENT: Taxi and private hire cross-border issues dominate Mansfield Council agenda
item.description: Taxi and private hire licensing will be a central focus when Mansfield District Council’s Licensing Committee meets on 22 January, with councillors set to review enforcement activity, complaint trends and the growing impact of national reform proposals on local control. item.title: Tom the Taxi Driver explains London’s soiling charges and why passengers might be subjected to the £60 fee
item.description: Passengers who are sick inside a London taxi can be charged a soiling fee on top of the fare, a practice drivers say reflects unavoidable cleaning costs and lost working time rather than a discretionary penalty. The issue has been set out in a recent video by Tom Hutley, known online as Tom the Taxi Driver, who explains how London cabbies deal with sick or other messy incidents during a shift. item.title: Bolt submits data showing out-of-area private hire drivers receive FEWER complaints compared to drivers working their licensed area
item.description: Ride-hailing operator Bolt has submitted further written evidence to the Transport Select Committee, setting out data and policy arguments in support of cross-border private hire work and warning against tighter geographic restrictions in any future reform of taxi and private hire licensing. The submission follows Bolt’s oral evidence session during the Committee’s inquiry into taxi and private hire licensing standards. item.title: Private hire driver drops appeal after falsely claiming wife was driving licensed vehicle during speeding incident
item.description: A private hire taxi driver has withdrawn his appeal against the revocation of his licence after admitting he falsely claimed his wife was driving when his vehicle was caught speeding on the M1. Gebrebrahan Nayzgi, who had been licensed in Bradford, was recorded exceeding the speed limit on the M1 near Sheffield on 26 May. item.description: Image screenshot credit: Baidu Baidu has launched a fully autonomous commercial ride-hailing service in Abu Dhabi through its Apollo Go platform, marking one of the Middle East’s first large-scale public deployments of driverless taxis. item.title: ‘TRADE MUST MAINTAIN REPUTATION’: Unite Glasgow Cab Section backs step up in taxi overcharging enforcement against rogue cabbies
item.description: Unite the Union’s Glasgow Cab Section has backed Glasgow City Council’s decision to refuse a taxi driver a new licence following overcharging complaints, supporting tougher enforcement to protect the trade’s reputation and passenger confidence. item.title: Taxi driver seriously injured in West Dorset collision as police appeal for witnesses
item.description: Dorset Police are appealing for witnesses and dashcam footage following a serious road traffic collision in West Dorset that left a taxi driver with significant injuries. Officers said they received a report at 4.09pm on Thursday 8 January 2026 of a collision involving a red Mitsubishi and a taxi on the A356 at South Perrot. item.description: The House of Commons Transport Committee formally challenged the Government to provide further detail on its plans to introduce national minimum standards for taxi and private hire vehicle licensing, ahead of a key evidence session last week.
